lede: The biggest thing to track this week is Tuesday's Telluride Town Council meeting, where a public hearing is scheduled on extending a project's vesting period — a real land-use decision with a public comment opportunity. The same morning, Council takes up automated license plate reader cameras, a privacy-versus-public-safety conversation worth paying attention to. Elsewhere, the town's 2027 General Fund and Capital budget get their first serious shape in a Wednesday work session, and the Ouray County Planning Commission digs into possible Land Use Code definition changes at the 4-H Event Center on Tuesday.

notable.stake: Public hearing on project vesting extension; ALPR camera debate raises privacy questions.
2027 General Fund and Capital budget contours set here before formal adoption.
